questions.question_text: Which of the following dienes can undergo Diels-Alder reaction most readily

questions.question_text: Separating techniques such as gas chromatography and liquid chromatography are not appropriate for separation of amino acids. Select correct reason from the following

options.B: Amino acids are low polarity substances
options.C: Amino acids are non polar substances

questions.explanation: Amino acids are zwitterionic and highly polar, making them poorly volatile for standard GC and requiring specialized LC conditions.

questions.question_text: When trans-2-butene is treated with bromine an anti-addition of bromine yields meso-2,3-dibromobutane. Select the correct statement regarding the reaction from the following

options.A: The reaction is stereoselective as well as stereo specific
options.B: The reaction is stereoselective and not stereo specific
options.C: The reaction is nonstereoselective as well as non stereo specific
options.D: The reaction is stereo specific and not stereo selection

questions.explanation: The reaction yields a specific stereoisomer from a specific stereoisomer via anti-addition, making it both stereoselective and stereospecific.

questions.question_text: Reduction of imines to give amines in protic solvents can be carried out by one of the following reagents. Select the correct reagent
questions.explanation: Sodium cyanoborohydride is a mild reducing agent commonly used for the reductive amination and selective reduction of imines in protic media.

questions.question_text: In the reaction of 2-nitrotoluene with bromine in presence of iron, which of the product shown below is the most abundant (major) product

options.A: Structure A with Br ortho/para to methyl and meta to nitro

questions.explanation: The methyl group is an activating ortho/para-director, directing incoming electrophiles preferentially relative to its position compared to the deactivating nitro group.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cannot react as a nucleophile
questions.explanation: Tetramethylammonium ion has a positive charge and a full octet with no lone pairs, so it cannot act as a nucleophile.

questions.question_text: Which of the following compounds will be oxidized by $CrO_3$ in acid
questions.explanation: Secondary alcohols like 2-methylcyclohexanol (often tested as ketone precursor) or related secondary positions are readily oxidized by chromium trioxide.

questions.question_text: Which of the following compounds absorbs at the longest wavelength
questions.explanation: Extended conjugation combined with phenyl rings increases the chain of conjugation, shifting absorption to longer wavelengths (bathochromic shift).

questions.question_text: Which of the following reagents will reduce a disubstituted alkyne to trans-alkene
questions.explanation: Dissolving metal reduction using sodium in liquid ammonia stereoselectively reduces alkynes to trans-alkenes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is true about following reaction: $H_3CO-C(H)(OH)-CH_2-Cl + OH^- \rightarrow S_2N$

options.A: The product will not have a stereo center
options.B: The product will have R configuration
options.C: The product will have S configuration
options.D: The reaction will happen with racemisation

questions.explanation: Nucleophilic substitution reactions involving chiral centers typically proceed with inversion or partial/full racemization depending on mechanism specifics.

questions.question_text: Which functional group is present in the molecule shown below (six-membered oxygen heterocycle, tetrahydropyran ring: C1CCOCC1)
questions.explanation: A cyclic ether linkage (C-O-C) represents the ether functional group.

questions.question_text: Match the following agents that cause cancer with the preferable sites for where it might cause: 1. Arsenic, 2. Benzene, 3. Cadmium Compounds, 4. Vinyl chloride
questions.explanation: Vinyl chloride is well known to cause hemangiosarcoma of the liver, benzene causes leukemia, and arsenic/cadmium affect specific target organs.

questions.question_text: If the pKa of lidocaine is 7.9 and pH of the infected tissue is 8.9, the fraction of drug in the ionized form will be
questions.explanation: Using Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for a weak base: pH - pKa = log([unionized]/[ionized]), 8.9 - 7.9 = 1 = log(10), meaning unionized/ionized = 10/1, so ionized fraction is 10%.

questions.question_text: Which among the following are the salient features of Glucocorticoids

options.A: Gets combined with highly specific cytosolic glucocorticoids
options.D: Increases lipid eicosanoids and prostaglandin gene

questions.explanation: Glucocorticoids exert their primary genomic actions by binding to specific intracellular cytosolic glucocorticoid receptors.

questions.question_text: The most commonly used test of sensitivity to antimicrobial agent is
questions.explanation: The Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method is the standard and most commonly used laboratory test for antimicrobial susceptibility.

questions.question_text: Bulk product is defined as

options.A: Product completing all processing stages but not necessarily final packing
options.B: A product ready for final dispatch
options.C: Raw material used for making final dosage form
options.D: A defined quantity of raw material from the same batch

questions.explanation: A bulk product has completed all processing stages up to, but not including, final packaging.

questions.question_text: Product, ....... and Promotion are four 'P's of marketing
questions.explanation: The traditional 4 Ps of marketing mix are Product, Price, Place, and Promotion.

questions.question_text: Insulin and thyroxin arrive at an organ / tissue / cell at the same time. Thyroxine causes an effect on the organ but insulin does not because

options.A: The organ cell have receptors for thyroxine but not for insulin
options.B: Thyroxin is a lipid-soluble hormone and insulin
options.C: The target cell in the organ have up-regulated for
options.D: Thyroxin is local hormone and insulin is a circula

questions.explanation: Thyroxine is lipophilic and can easily cross cell membranes to bind intracellular receptors, whereas insulin acts via membrane-bound receptors depending on tissue type.

questions.question_text: Which among the following is an incorrect statement with regard to the drug Dantrolene

options.D: It is a skeletal muscle relaxant

questions.explanation: Dantrolene contains a hydantoin ring attached to a nitrophenylfurfurylidene moiety, making statement A incorrect.

questions.question_text: Diazepam is not suitable for peroral sustained release form since

options.A: Is not absorbed in lower intestine
options.B: It has biological half life greater than twelve effects hour
options.C: It has biological half life less than one hour

questions.explanation: Diazepam has a long biological half-life (around 20-50 hours), making sustained-release peroral formulations unnecessary.

questions.question_text: Antioxidant used as blocking agent in sterile product is
questions.explanation: Sodium bisulfite is commonly used as an aqueous antioxidant and reducing agent in sterile parenteral formulations.

questions.explanation: Antihistamines are generally not effective as primary therapy in asthma because histamine plays a minor role in human bronchoconstriction compared to leukotrienes and other mediators.

questions.question_text: Match the following adrenergic drugs with their receptor affinity: (1) Epinephrine, (2) Noradreanline, (3) Phenylephrine, (4) Dobutamine

options.C: More beta 1 & beta 2, no alpha 1 and dopamine
options.D: More alpha 1 & beta 1, no beta 2 & dopamine

questions.question_text: If the drug substance has been substituted wholly or in part by another drug or substance, it is called as
questions.explanation: An adulterated drug legal definition includes substitution of any valuable constituent wholly or in part by another substance.

questions.question_text: One of the principle upon which HPLC detector functions is

options.A: Redox property of solute is the basis for functioning of Electrochemical detectors
options.B: Fluorimetric detector has high selectivity and low sensitivity
options.C: Small difference in Refractive Index of mobile phase permit precise measurements in Refractive index detectors
options.D: UV detector function based on its ability to detector

questions.explanation: Electrochemical detectors operate based on the oxidation or reduction (redox properties) of electroactive analytes at an electrode surface.

questions.question_text: Methanolic extract of a crude drug powder when treated with magnesium turnings and concentrated hydrochloric acid turned the solution magenta coloured. The test is termed as
questions.explanation: Shinoda test (Mg/HCl reduction test) is a characteristic qualitative chemical test for the identification of flavonoids.

questions.explanation: Etoposide and teniposide are semisynthetic glycoside derivatives of podophyllotoxin isolated from Podophyllum species.

questions.question_text: The thymus secretes several hormones related to the immunity. These hormones promote the maturation of T lymphocyte cells. These hormones are: 1. Thymosin, 2. Thymichumoral factor, 3. Thymic factor, 4. Interleukins
questions.explanation: Thymosin, thymichumoral factor, and thymic factor are known thymic hormones involved in T-cell maturation.

questions.question_text: For the measurement of particle size of powders, the distance measured between two tangents on opposite sides of the particle parallel to some fixed direction is called
questions.explanation: Feret's diameter is the distance between two parallel tangents on opposite sides of the particle image.

questions.question_text: Beta oxidation of fatty acids takes place in
questions.explanation: Beta-oxidation of fatty acids primarily occurs within the mitochondrial matrix of eukaryotic cells.

questions.question_text: Which of the following genera is not the source for tropane alkaloids
questions.explanation: Nicotiana species are the source of pyridine alkaloids (like nicotine), whereas Datura, Duboisia, and Atropa are sources of tropane alkaloids.

questions.question_text: The useful variable from in vitro dissolution test data for IVIVC includes
questions.explanation: Parameters like t50% or mean dissolution time are standard variables used to correlate in vitro data with in vivo pharmacokinetic profiles.

questions.question_text: In respect of female reproductive cycle, which of the following statements are correct: 1. The female reproductive cycle consists of menstrual phase, a pre-ovulatory phase, ovulation and a post ovulatory phase
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2, 3, and 6 correctly describe the physiological phases and events of the normal female ovarian and uterine cycles.

questions.question_text: Apparent volume of distribution will be highest in case of the drug with % plasmaprotein binding
questions.explanation: Lower plasma protein binding generally allows more free drug to distribute into peripheral tissues, increasing the apparent volume of distribution.

questions.question_text: To rule out the probability of dose dumping from an oral CR dosage form, USP hasincluded which sampling time point for in vitro dissolution test where D is normal dosing interval
questions.explanation: An early time point such as 0.50D (half of the dosing interval) is typically specified in USP dissolution tests for controlled-release products to detect potential dose dumping.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement regarding cerebral hemisphere is true

options.A: The right and left hemisphere are symmetrical
options.B: This right more important for spoken and written language
options.C: The left hemisphere is more important for musical and artistic awareness
options.D: Hemispheric lateralization is more pronounced in male than in female

questions.explanation: Neuroscience studies indicate that functional lateralization of the cerebral hemispheres tends to be more pronounced in males than in females.

questions.question_text: Which among the following is a Class-I method, used for rendering a solution of drug isotonic with body fluids
questions.explanation: The White-Vincent method is classified as a Class I method for adjusting tonicity and calculating sodium chloride equivalents.

questions.question_text: (Weight in pounds/150) * Adult Dose = Child dose. The above formula is known as _______ in Posology
questions.explanation: Clarke's formula calculates pediatric dosage based on the child's weight in pounds divided by 150 multiplied by the adult dose.

questions.question_text: The type of particle diameter obtained by microscopic method of evaluation is
questions.explanation: Microscopic evaluation typically measures the projected diameter of particles based on their visual area under the microscope.

questions.question_text: Naphazoline

options.A: Is used for relief of nasal congestion

questions.question_text: A patient receiving warfarin develops rheumatoid arthritis. Which one of the following drugs would be Contraindicated
questions.explanation: Aspirin causes significant GI ulceration risk and inhibits platelet function, severely compounding the bleeding risks associated with warfarin anticoagulation.

questions.explanation: Glycogen storage disease, Gilbert's syndrome, hemochromatosis, and Wilson's disease are inherited metabolic disorders directly impacting liver function and deposition.

options.B: Drug absorption by these routes by pass first pass metabolism
options.C: There is an optimum log P for sublingual absorption

questions.question_text: Which among the following statements describing surface activity for surfactants is incorrect

questions.question_text: The Michaelis-Menten hypothesis

options.C: States that the rate of a chemical reaction maybe independent of substrate concentration

questions.question_text: Which of the following techniques is not useful to detect polymorphs

questions.question_text: Which of the following constituents is responsible for colour of shellac

questions.question_text: Match the following drugs with alteration they produces in structural-functional of kidney: (1) Aminoglycoside Antibiotics (2) ACE inhibitors (3) Methotrexate (4) NSAIDs with (A) Glomerular abnormality (B) Tubular epithelial cell Damage (C) Hemodynamic Mediated kidney injury (D) Obstructive nephropathy

questions.question_text: Hixon Crowell's cube root law of dissolution states that

options.A: There is a change in particle size and surface area during dissolution of drug
options.B: Dissolution process is controlled by diffusion of molecules/ions
options.C: High free energy of activation is required for solution

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding estrogen therapy in postmenopausal women are true EXCEPT

questions.question_text: Chapter IV of which law states that experiments on animals are avoided wherever it is possible to do so...
